title: 6-Month Exam Path
lede: 26 weeks, about 5 hours a week, from your first day to passing CON 3990V. Each week has a short goal, a few tasks, a FAR reading and a 10-question check. Each month ends with a timed checkpoint. It follows the order of your courses and the official exam blueprint, and every question was checked against the RFO FAR in force since the exam was updated on 31 March 2026.
how: **About 5 hours a week.** 30 to 45 minutes on weekdays (a lesson, the FAR reading, 10 flashcards), plus one longer block on the weekend for the weekly check.
**Do the tasks in order.** Lessons and drills tick themselves when you finish them. Tick FAR readings and other tasks yourself.
**Score the checks honestly.** Each month ends with a timed checkpoint. Hit the target before you move on; if you miss, repeat the month's drills and retake it.
**Behind? Do not skip the checkpoint.** Push the next week's reading instead. The checkpoints are what tell you whether you are ready.
**Your dates follow your plan.** The path starts on your start date in My plan and stretches if your goal is longer than 6 months.

months.title: Foundation
months.sub: How the FAR works, who can bind the Government, ethics and money rules. Course: CON 1100V.

months.title: Pre-award
months.sub: Requirements, market research, competition, contract types, commercial buys and publicizing. Course: CON 1200V and the five online modules.

months.title: Post-award, then pricing
months.sub: Running the contract, quality, changes, disputes, terminations, closeout, then price and cost analysis. Course: CON 1400V.

months.title: Award
months.sub: Source selection, negotiation, award, debriefings and protests. Courses: CON 1300V and CON 7300V.

months.title: Review and close the gaps
months.sub: Your class practice exam, the RFO changes, CON 3910, register for the exam and the first full simulation.

months.title: Test-ready
months.sub: Fix weak areas, a second full simulation, exam week and what comes after.

weeks.title: Start strong: the exam and how the FAR works
weeks.goal: Know what CON 3990V looks like, get your first course on the calendar, and learn how the FAR is organized.

tasks.d: 150 questions, 3 hours, 70% to pass, closed book. Know the four areas and how many questions each gets.
Focus on 1.102 (the seven guiding principles), 1.107 (FAR conventions) and subpart 1.3 (deviations).
Use AITAS. Ask your training office which class dates fit.

tasks.t: Flashcards: FAR part titles on the exam
tasks.d: Do 10 cards a day until you know all 20.

weeks.tip: Read the FAR with a question in mind. Open Part 1, find 1.107 and ask: what does it tell me about thresholds, delegation and words like "shall"?
weeks.class: Day 1 of the B2B class covered the exam format, the 20 FAR parts, the UCF, forms and PIIDs. The class slides cite FAR 1.108 for the conventions and subpart 1.4 for deviations; under the RFO they are FAR 1.107 and subpart 1.3.

weeks.title: Authority: who can bind the Government
weeks.goal: Explain actual versus apparent authority, what a warrant is, what a COR can and cannot do, and how ratification works.

tasks.d: 1.402-1 (authority), 1.402-2 (responsibilities), 1.403-2 (the SF 1402 warrant), 1.404 (COR), 1.405 (ratification).
Contract, offer, shall/may/should, claim, solicitation provision and contract clause, micro-purchase and simplified acquisition thresholds.

weeks.tip: Authority questions are usually scenarios. Ask one thing first: did the person who acted have a written warrant covering this action? If not, nothing binds the Government until ratification.
weeks.class: The class taught that apparent authority is not recognized and that only actual authority (express or implied) binds the Government. That is still right. The CO authority section is now FAR 1.402-1 (it was 1.602-1).

weeks.title: What makes a contract, and the money rules
weeks.goal: Name the elements of a contract, tell a provision from a clause, and explain purpose, time and amount under the Antideficiency Act.

tasks.d: Contracts conditioned on availability of funds and the limitation of cost and funds clauses.

weeks.tip: For money questions, sort the problem into Purpose (right appropriation), Time (bona fide need, period of availability) or Amount (not more than you have). Most ADA questions fall into one of the three.
weeks.class: Day 1 listed four elements of a contract: capacity, mutual assent, consideration and lawful purpose. Day 5 taught the ADA's three provisions (time, purpose, amount). Both are still right.

weeks.title: Ethics, the contract file and remedies. Month 1 checkpoint
weeks.goal: Spot conflicts of interest and procurement integrity problems, know what goes in a contract file and how long it is kept, and read a PIID.

tasks.d: Standards of conduct, gratuities, and procurement integrity.
Contract files, the PIID (Table 4-1), closeout time standards (Table 4-2) and retention (Table 4-3).

weeks.tip: Checkpoint target: 60%. You have not finished the courses yet, so this checks the habit, not the score. Review every miss in the results.
weeks.class: Day 5 cited FAR 4.801 and 4.802 for contract files. Under the RFO, contract file contents are FAR 4.101 and retention is FAR 4.309: keep contracts 6 years after final payment.

weeks.title: Describing the need and market research
weeks.goal: Tell a SOW from a PWS and SOO, and know when market research is required and what it decides.

tasks.d: One section now (10.001): the three times market research is required and the order of priority for commercial solutions.
Describing agency needs.
Do the pre-work before day one.

tasks.t: Weekly check: requirements and market research

weeks.tip: When a question asks what market research is for, think priority order: existing governmentwide contract, modify the requirement to fit one, another commercial source, modified commercial, then nondevelopmental (10.001(f)).
weeks.class: Day 1 taught strategic and tactical market research. The RFO's Part 10 is short but still requires market research before new requirements, before solicitations over the SAT, and before task or delivery orders over the SAT.

weeks.title: Required sources, small business and competition
weeks.goal: Know where to look first, when to set aside for small business, the seven exceptions to full and open competition, and who approves a justification.

tasks.d: 6.101 (competitive procedures), 6.103-1 to 6.103-7 (the seven exceptions), 6.104 (justifications), 6.301 (posting the justification).
19.000(b) (where Part 19 applies, changed by the RFO) and the rule of two.

tasks.t: Weekly check: sources, small business, competition

weeks.tip: Memorize the seven exceptions in order: one source, urgency, industrial mobilization/expert, international agreement, statute, national security, public interest. Then learn which two need no justification (statute and public interest).
weeks.class: Day 1 listed the seven CICA exceptions; they are now FAR 6.103-1 through 6.103-7 (they were 6.302-x). Exam-taker notes ask about small business stateside versus overseas: under the RFO, Part 19 must apply in the U.S. and may apply outside it.

weeks.title: Planning, contract types and choosing the method
weeks.goal: Match a situation to the right contract type and the right buying method, from micro-purchase to negotiation.

tasks.d: Selecting a contract type, when FFP must be used, and when cost-reimbursement is allowed.

tasks.t: Weekly check: planning, types and methods

weeks.tip: Contract type questions turn on risk. Clear, stable requirement with good price history: FFP. Requirement you cannot define: cost-reimbursement. A 4th production lot of a mature missile is the classic FFP case.
weeks.class: Day 3 showed cost risk shifting from fixed-price (small variance) to cost-reimbursement (large variance). Exam-taker notes say a mature 4th production lot is FFP. Both still hold (FAR 16.102(c), 16.202-2).

weeks.title: Commercial buys, publicizing and the UCF. Month 2 checkpoint
weeks.goal: Know the RFO's commercial rules (Part 12), notice and response times (Part 5), and every UCF section from A to M.

tasks.d: 12.101 to 12.104, 12.201-1 (simplified procedures to $9 million), 12.205 (provisions and clauses), 12.304 (terminations) and subpart 12.4 (micro-purchases).
Table 5-2 (notice times), Table 5-3 (response times) and Table 5-4 (award notices).

tasks.t: Finish the five online modules for CON 1300V
tasks.d: FAC 069, FAC 082, FAC 085, CON 0074 and CON 0470. Save every certificate.

weeks.tip: Make a one-page sheet: >$20K to $25K post 10 days; >$25K notice 15 days before the solicitation; >SAT noncommercial 30 days to respond; R&D 45 days from the notice. Commercial over the SAT: a combined synopsis/solicitation with a reasonable response time.
weeks.class: Day 3's publicizing chart starts at $10K and Day 4 says commercial buys have three standard provisions and two clauses. Under the RFO the posting floor is $20K, and 52.212-3 and 52.212-5 are reserved: 12.205 requires 52.212-1 and 52.212-4, adds 52.212-2 when needed, and lists the rest in tables.

weeks.title: Running the contract and quality
weeks.goal: Know what contract administration covers, the postaward orientation, CPARS, inspection at source or destination, acceptance, and who carries the risk of loss.

tasks.d: Contract administration functions (including postaward orientation), stop-work orders and CPARS.
Nonconformance classes, source versus destination, acceptance and risk of loss.
When the Government furnishes property and when contractors are liable for its loss.
It needs only CON 1100V, so it can fill a gap while you wait for CON 1300V.

weeks.tip: Risk of loss questions: find the f.o.b. point. Origin: risk passes at the carrier. Destination: at acceptance or delivery, whichever is later. After acceptance, the Government owns the problem unless the defect was latent.
weeks.class: Watch out: the Day 5 slide on nonconformances swaps minor and major. Major means likely to fail or to materially reduce usability; minor means not likely to (FAR 46.101). The light-bulb scenario test takers reported is a risk-of-loss question (46.505).

weeks.title: Subcontracts, changes and modifications
weeks.goal: Tell a bilateral from a unilateral modification every time, and know how change orders, scope and equitable adjustments work.

tasks.d: 43.201 (administrative change), 43.202 (only COs modify), 43.203 (bilateral and unilateral), 43.204 (contractor notice), subpart 43.3 (change orders) and 43.401 (SF 30).
Consent to subcontract and privity.

weeks.tip: One test taker had about 10 questions on bilateral versus unilateral. Rule of thumb: if the contractor must agree (price, new terms, extra work by agreement), it is bilateral. If a clause gives the Government the right (changes, options, admin, funding, termination notice), it is unilateral.
weeks.class: Day 5's list (bilateral: definitize letter contracts and other agreements; unilateral: admin changes, funding, change orders, termination notices) matches the RFO's FAR 43.203. Duty to proceed after a change order is now 43.301(b).

weeks.title: Disputes, terminations and closeout
weeks.goal: Walk a claim from final decision to appeal, choose the right termination, and know the closeout time standards.

tasks.d: Claims, certification over $100,000, the final decision, and the 90-day / 12-month appeal clocks.
When Part 49 does not apply (commercial), notice of termination, cure and show cause notices.

weeks.tip: Three terminations: convenience (Government no longer needs it), default (noncommercial, contractor at fault, Part 49), cause (commercial, contractor at fault, 52.212-4(m)). Cure notice when 10 or more days remain; show cause when fewer.
weeks.class: Day 4's slides on claims, appeals (90 days to the ASBCA, 12 months to the Court of Federal Claims) and terminations are still right. The closeout times on Day 1 match the RFO's Table 4-2.

weeks.title: Price analysis
weeks.goal: Choose the right price analysis technique and decide whether a price is fair and reasonable.

tasks.d: When to use price, cost and cost realism analysis, and the price analysis techniques (the first two are preferred).

weeks.tip: Price analysis looks at the total price; cost analysis looks at the pieces. If certified data are not required, you must do price analysis (15.404(a)(2)).
weeks.class: Day 3's definitions of price, cost, cost realism and technical analysis, unit prices and unbalanced pricing all still match FAR 15.404.

weeks.title: Cost analysis and certified data. Month 3 checkpoint
weeks.goal: Know when certified cost or pricing data are required and prohibited, and the basic cost principles.

tasks.d: Prohibitions and exceptions, the threshold, and the certificate.
Allowability, direct costs and indirect costs.

weeks.tip: Checkpoint target: 70%, the real passing score. Certified data: never at or below the SAT; required at $2.5 million under the FAR and above $10 million for DoW contracts awarded after 30 June 2026, unless an exception applies.
weeks.class: The class practice exam said certified data are required over $2 million. That is out of date: the FAR figure is $2.5 million, and DoW's is $10 million for awards after 30 June 2026.

weeks.title: Source selection
weeks.goal: Pick the right source selection approach, follow the RFO exchange rules (clarifications and negotiations), and document the decision.

tasks.d: 15.103 (tradeoff, LPTA, highest technically rated, phased), 15.104 (factors), 15.106 (amendments), 15.107 (late proposals), 15.109 (UCF).
SSA duties, clarifications, competitive range, negotiations and the source selection decision.

weeks.tip: The exam FAQ says to read Part 15 thoroughly. Learn the RFO flow: receipt, evaluation (clarifications as needed), competitive range, negotiations, proposal revisions, decision, award, notices, debriefings.
weeks.class: Big RFO change: the class taught three exchanges (clarifications, communications, discussions). Under the RFO there are two: clarifications (FAR 15.202(a)(2)) and negotiations with the competitive range (15.204-2). "Communications" before the competitive range no longer exists as a separate step.

weeks.title: Negotiation
weeks.goal: Plan a negotiation, set objectives, and document the result in a price negotiation memorandum.

tasks.d: Price negotiation, prenegotiation objectives and documenting the negotiation.
Required since 1 October 2026, after CON 1300V. Brush up on Excel first.

weeks.tip: Know which document goes where: prenegotiation objectives before you negotiate, the price negotiation memorandum after (15.408), and a memo for record for a no-cost change.
weeks.class: One test taker was unsure whether a no-cost change (moving a door) belongs in a PNM or a memo for record. The rule: a negotiated price goes in a PNM (FAR 15.408-2); a change with no price effect can be recorded in a memo for record in the contract file.

weeks.title: Award, notices and debriefings
weeks.goal: Know the award documents, the notices to unsuccessful offerors, and the pre- and postaward debriefing rules and deadlines.

tasks.d: Preaward notices and debriefings, award, award notice in 3 days, postaward debriefing (request in 3 days, held within 5).

weeks.tip: Postaward orientation (with the winner, about running the contract) and postaward debriefing (with offerors, about the evaluation) are different things. Test takers say the exam checks that.
weeks.class: Day 4's debriefing rules (request within 3 days, debrief within 5) are still right; they are now FAR 15.301-1. The FAR now says COs may allow follow-up questions if time permits (15.301-2); the DFARS follow-up rule the slide cites (215.506-70) should be checked against DoW's current deviation.

weeks.title: Protests. Month 4 checkpoint
weeks.goal: Know the three protest forums, the filing deadlines, the stay rules, and your first actions when a protest arrives.

tasks.d: 33.102 (definitions), 33.103 (consult counsel first), 33.104 (agency protests, 35 days), 33.105 (GAO, stays).

weeks.tip: Protest timing in one line: solicitation problems before closing; everything else at GAO within 10 days of knowing; issues from a required debriefing within 5 days of it; stay if filed within 10 days of award or 5 days of the debriefing.
weeks.class: Day 4's protest material (three forums, agency 35 days, GAO 100 days) is still right. The RFO adds that the CO should consult legal counsel on learning of a protest (FAR 33.103(a)).

weeks.title: Your class practice exam, updated for the RFO
weeks.goal: Work through the B2B class practice exam, now corrected for the RFO, and read what changed.

tasks.d: What the class materials say, what the FAR says now, and why some answers changed.

weeks.tip: Read every explanation, including on the questions you got right. The class versions that were wrong under the RFO say what changed.
weeks.class: 143 questions from the class practice exam were checked: 91 still right as written, 38 updated (new FAR numbers, thresholds or wording) and 14 fixed (wrong or unclear under the RFO). A few true/false items that repeated other questions were dropped.

weeks.title: The RFO changes, and what test takers saw
weeks.goal: Lock in the FAR Overhaul changes the exam now tests, and drill the topics past test takers reported.

tasks.t: Read FAR & key numbers: What changed lately
tasks.d: Old and new FAR numbers, thresholds and deadlines.
What people who took CON 3990V say to know, checked against the RFO.

weeks.tip: About 30% of the exam bank was rewritten for the RFO on 31 March 2026. Old study guides, slides and practice tests that use pre-RFO numbers can still teach the concept, but trust the RFO cite.
weeks.class: Test takers said the exam felt about 80% scenario and 20% straight recall. That matches the way this path drills: understand the concept, then apply it.

weeks.title: CON 3910 and the missed-question sweep
weeks.goal: Finish WarU's online exam prep and clear your missed-question list.
weeks.tip: Guiding Principles is the biggest area: 42 of 150 questions. If your readiness there is under 70%, spend an extra session on lessons L01 to L08.
weeks.class: Test takers recommend memorizing the 20 FAR part titles; some questions just ask which part covers a topic.

weeks.title: Register for the exam. First full simulation
weeks.goal: Get your exam on the calendar and take your first full 150-question simulation under real conditions.

tasks.t: Apply for CON 3990V and book a test center
tasks.d: AITAS, then the Pearson Authorization to Test (schedule within 90 days). Test centers pass about 4% more than online testing.

weeks.tip: Take the simulation in one sitting, closed book, at the time of day your exam is booked. Target 75%: real-exam nerves cost a few points.
weeks.class: Day 1 said the exam is 150 multiple-choice questions, 70% to pass, and that about 10 are unscored test questions. The official FAQ confirms 150 questions and 70%.

weeks.title: Fix your weakest area
weeks.goal: Use your readiness scores to spend this week where the points are.

tasks.t: Redo the lessons for your weakest area
tasks.d: Open Lessons and filter by the area with the lowest readiness.

tasks.t: Flashcards: FAR part titles, final pass

weeks.tip: Look at the four bars on this page. Raising your weakest area from 60% to 75% is worth more than polishing your best one.
weeks.class: Your Pearson score report shows the same four areas, so this is how you would study for a retake too.

weeks.title: Second full simulation
weeks.goal: Prove you are ready: two full simulations at 75% or better.

tasks.d: ID, arrival time, breaks, what you may bring.

weeks.tip: If you are under 70% on this simulation, talk to your supervisor about moving the exam date. Up to three attempts in 12 months are allowed, but each one should count.
weeks.class: Test takers say understanding the concept beats memorizing answers. If a simulation question surprises you, read the lesson, not just the explanation.

weeks.title: Exam week
weeks.goal: Stay sharp without cramming, and take CON 3990V.

tasks.t: Flashcards: Key numbers, one last look

tasks.d: Record your score in Certification 101 → The exam.

weeks.tip: The night before: no new material. On the exam, answer every question (no penalty for guessing), flag the long ones, and come back.
weeks.class: Exam facts from the class and the official FAQ: 150 questions, 3 hours, closed book, 70% to pass.

weeks.title: After the exam
weeks.goal: Passed: start the certification paperwork. Not yet: build the retake plan.

tasks.t: Passed? Line up your certification application
tasks.d: You still need 12 months of full-time experience. Keep your experience checklist up to date.
At least 30 days between attempts, up to three in 12 months. After a first failure you must take CON 3900V. Use your score report's four areas to aim your study.

weeks.tip: Tick whichever task applies to you and leave the other.
weeks.class: Retake rules and CON 3900V come from the official exam FAQ, not the class materials.

weeks.title: Finish line
weeks.goal: Courses and exam done. Keep learning on the job.

tasks.d: Mark your courses and exam done so your timeline shows what is left.
Share this guide with the next new 51C or 1102 in your office.

weeks.tip: Certification needs the courses, the exam and 12 months of experience. You have done the hardest part.

files.name: Back To Basics Day One (slides)
files.what: Exam format, blueprint, the 20 FAR parts, UCF, common forms, PIID, life cycle, contract principles, how to read the FAR.

files.name: Back to Basics Prep Day 3 (slides)
files.what: Offers and quotations, solicitation types, contract types, types of analysis, cost elements, Part 15 exchanges, publicizing times.

files.name: Back to Basics Prep Day 4 (slides)
files.what: Debriefings, protests, disputes and claims, terminations, commercial provisions and clauses, Part 15 review, CBAR.

files.name: Back to Basics Prep Day 5 (slides)
files.what: Post-award: roles, orientation, CPARS, files, changes, funds, quality, payments, closeout.

files.name: Back to Basics final (practice exam)
files.what: About 150 practice questions, no answer key. Every one was answered and checked; 143 are in this guide, rewritten where the RFO changed them.

files.name: Jeopardy B2B review (slides)
files.what: 30 review questions in six categories, no answers. Answered and checked; now the B2B Jeopardy flashcard deck.

files.name: Pop quiz: FAR parts
files.what: Match 21 descriptions to FAR parts. Covered by the FAR part flashcards and the FAR Part Match game (RFO titles).

files.name: Study Guide for Exam (test-taker notes)
files.what: Topic lists from people who took the exam. Each topic is checked under Test-taker tips.

files.name: CON 3990V (test-taker notes)
files.what: One test taker's recalled topics and advice. Checked under Test-taker tips; recalled exam questions are not copied.

files.name: Contracting Study Guide V9 (19 May 2025)
files.what: Protected with an Army Microsoft Purview sensitivity label, so it could not be opened outside an authorized Army account. Not reviewed. If its label allows sharing, open it on your Army computer and save an unprotected copy; otherwise keep it out of this guide.

checks.said: 150 questions from a pool of about 600, multiple choice, 70% to pass, about 10 unscored trial questions.
checks.now: 150 questions, 3 hours, 70%, closed book (official exam FAQ). The pool size and unscored items are not in the FAQ.

checks.said: Guiding Principles 42, Pre-Award 30, Award 40, Post-Award 38, by competency.
checks.now: Same counts in the official blueprint.
Same list in the exam FAQ. RFO titles changed for Part 13 (Simplified Procedures for Noncommercial Acquisitions) and Part 19 (Small Business).

checks.said: FAR 1.108, including a rule on tense and voice and "imperative sentences".
checks.now: Now FAR 1.107. Paragraphs: words and terms, delegation, dollar thresholds, applying FAR changes, citations, and "required action". There is no tense rule.

checks.said: FAR subpart 1.4 (and 1.108(d) in one question).
checks.now: FAR subpart 1.3: definition 1.301, individual 1.303, class 1.304.

checks.said: 1.102(a): deliver best value on a timely basis, maintain public trust, fulfill public policy objectives.
checks.now: Replaced by seven guiding principles: mission first, effective use of taxpayer dollars, maximize commercial, award to contractors with a superior ability to perform, competition, integrity, and decisions at the lowest level.

checks.said: Contracting officer responsibilities are in FAR subpart 1.6.
checks.now: Now subpart 1.4: 1.402-1 authority, 1.402-2 responsibilities, 1.403-2 SF 1402 appointment, 1.404 COR, 1.405 ratification.

checks.said: Defined in FAR 1.108(a).
checks.now: "Shall denotes the imperative" is a Part 2 definition (2.101); 1.107(a) says Part 2 definitions apply everywhere.

checks.said: FAR 2.101's definition of offer says RFQ responses are quotations, not offers.
checks.now: The RFO shortened the 2.101 definition. The quotation rule is now in 12.201-1(b): a quotation is not an offer, and the purchase order is the Government's offer.

checks.said: SF 33 = sealed bid; DD 1409 = abstract of offers.
checks.now: The SF 33 (Solicitation, Offer and Award) is used for sealed bids and RFPs. The abstract of offers is the SF 1409 (FAR 14.303(g)). The others on the list are right.

checks.said: 13 characters: office (1-6), fiscal year (7-8), type (9), 4-digit number (10-13).
checks.now: 13 to 17 characters: the serial number can be 4 to 8 characters, no hyphens. Table 4-1 letters unchanged. Now FAR 4.201.
Contents: FAR 4.101. Retention: 4.309, Table 4-3 (contracts 6 years after final payment).

checks.said: SAP on receipt and final payment; FFP 6 months; indirect rates 36 months; all others 20 months.
checks.now: Same, in FAR 4.308-2, Table 4-2.

checks.said: Defined in FAR 4.804-4.
checks.now: The RFO Part 4 dropped that definition, but the idea is unchanged: closeout starts on evidence of physical completion (4.308-2(a)).

checks.said: Post $10K to $25K for 10 days; notices 15 days before the solicitation above $25K; 30 days to respond above the SAT; 45 days for R&D.
checks.now: Posting floor is now over $20,000 (10 days to $25,000). The rest holds: Tables 5-2 and 5-3. Below the SAT no separate notice is needed if the solicitation is posted on SAM.gov with electronic responses.

checks.said: Vendors get 45 days to respond to a noncommercial solicitation.
checks.now: At least 30 days from the solicitation (Table 5-3), after a notice at least 15 days before it, so at least 45 days from notice to closing. R&D: 45 days from the notice.

checks.said: Post a pre-notification on the GPE over $20K.
checks.now: Correct under the RFO: post a presolicitation notice on SAM.gov for actions over $20,000 unless exempt (5.101(a)).

checks.said: FAR 5.202 exceptions; urgency lets you shorten the synopsis time (5.203).
checks.now: Exemptions are in 5.101(b). Other-than-full-and-open authorities are exempt except only-one-source and national security; urgency needs no notice, and its justification is posted within 30 days after award.

checks.said: Seven exceptions at FAR 6.302-1 to 6.302-7.
checks.now: Same seven, renumbered 6.103-1 to 6.103-7. Justifications are 6.104; posting 6.301.

checks.said: Limited-sources justification under FAR 8.405-6.
checks.now: FAR 8.401(b) now sends schedule ordering to GSA's procedures (GSAR 538.71), which keep the limited-sources justification.

checks.said: All SAP is in Part 13; commercial SAP up to $7.5 million; oral solicitations allowed under 13.106-1.
checks.now: Part 13 is now noncommercial only, at or below the SAT. Commercial simplified procedures: 12.201-1, up to $9 million ($15 million in special cases). Micro-purchases: subpart 12.4. The RFO dropped the oral-quotation text.

checks.said: Know the SAT, micro-purchase and commercial SAP thresholds.
checks.now: Micro-purchase $15,000; SAT $350,000; commercial simplified procedures $9 million (October 2025 inflation adjustment).

checks.said: Three standard provisions (52.212-1, -2, -3) and two clauses (52.212-4, -5) under FAR 12.301.
checks.now: 52.212-3 and 52.212-5 are reserved under the RFO. 12.205 requires 52.212-1 and 52.212-4, adds 52.212-2 when using other procedures, and lists other provisions and clauses in Tables 12-2 and 12-3.

checks.said: 52.212-4(l) convenience and (m) cause; procedures in FAR 12.403.
checks.now: Same paragraphs; procedures now FAR 12.304, which says not to use Part 49.

checks.said: Every commercial modification must be bilateral under 52.212-4.
checks.now: Changes to the terms need written agreement of both parties (52.212-4(d)). Administrative changes and actions under other clauses, such as options, can still be unilateral.

checks.said: Required under FAR 14.201-1 and 15.204-1.
checks.now: IFBs use it to the maximum practicable extent (14.201-1); RFPs should use it (15.102(b)), with listed exceptions. The format itself is 15.109.

checks.said: Sections A to M in four parts.
checks.now: Same. Part IV (K, L, M) is not physically included in the contract; Section K is incorporated by reference.

checks.said: Three exchanges: clarifications, communications (before the competitive range), discussions.
checks.now: Two: clarifications (any time after receipt to award, no revisions) and negotiations with offerors in the competitive range. Communications is gone as a separate step.

checks.said: All of the most highly rated proposals.
checks.now: The proposals best suited for further negotiation; may be narrowed to the most highly rated for efficiency.

checks.said: LPTA and tradeoff (and a "best value continuum").
checks.now: Tradeoff, LPTA, highest technically rated with a fair and reasonable price (new), and phased acquisition.

Renumbered: early exchanges 15.101; receipt 15.107-15.108; clarifications 15.202(a)(2); competitive range 15.204-1; negotiations and revisions 15.204-2; decision 15.205; preaward notices and debriefing 15.206; award and notice 15.207; postaward debriefing 15.301.

checks.said: Request within 3 days, debrief within 5; DFARS 215.506-70 follow-up questions (2 and 5 business days).
checks.now: 3 and 5 days are still right (15.206-2, 15.301-1). The FAR now lets COs allow follow-up questions if time permits (15.301-2). Check the DFARS follow-up rule against DoW's current deviation.

checks.said: Required over $2 million.
checks.now: $2.5 million under the FAR; $10 million for DoW contracts awarded after 30 June 2026. Never at or below the SAT.

checks.said: Resolicit for 30 days unless an exception applies.
checks.now: Still DoW policy: DFARS 215.371-2, which the DoW RFO deviation for Part 14 also points to.

checks.said: Price, cost, cost realism, technical analysis; unit prices; unbalanced pricing.
checks.now: Same, in FAR 15.404 to 15.404-6.

checks.said: Three forums; agency about 35 days; GAO 100 days (65 express); CO's first action?
checks.now: Same. The RFO adds: consult legal counsel on learning of a protest (33.103(a)) and notify the HCA of an agency protest.

checks.said: Claim certified over $100,000; final decision; ASBCA 90 days; Court of Federal Claims 12 months; keep performing.
Agencies are encouraged to use ADR. Voluntary or required?
checks.now: Voluntary by definition (33.201).

checks.said: Most effective when held promptly after award (old subpart 42.5).
checks.now: Still a contract administration function (42.302(a)(3)), but the RFO removed the detailed orientation subpart; 42.5 is now indirect cost rates.

checks.said: Used over the SAT; can a contractor protest a rating?
checks.now: Evaluations are required over the SAT, at least annually and at completion. Contractors get 14 days to comment; disagreements go to a level above the CO. A rating is not protestable.

checks.said: Changes clauses 52.243-1 to -7; within general scope; 30 days to assert an adjustment; duty to proceed.
checks.now: Same. Change orders are now subpart 43.3, and the duty to proceed is 43.301(b).

checks.said: Minor = likely to materially reduce usability; major = likely to result in failure.
checks.now: Wrong on the slide. Major = likely to fail OR materially reduce usability; minor = NOT likely to materially reduce usability; critical = hazardous or unsafe.

checks.said: FAR 46.402 and 46.403 lists.
checks.now: Same section numbers and lists.

checks.said: Bulbs accepted, then found broken: the Government is responsible.
checks.now: Correct: risk passes at acceptance or delivery at destination, whichever is later; acceptance is conclusive except for latent defects, fraud or gross mistakes.

checks.said: Contractors are not liable for damaged GFP unless it is an FFP contract.
checks.now: Close: not liable under cost-reimbursement, T&M, labor-hour, and fixed-price contracts priced on certified cost or pricing data. Other fixed-price contracts: generally liable.

checks.said: 30 days after a proper invoice (15 days for small business).
checks.now: 30 days is the Prompt Payment Act due date. 15 days for small business is an accelerated-payment goal, not a new deadline.

checks.said: If a contractor asks for advance payments, look at other financing first.
checks.now: Correct: advance payments are last in the order of preference.

checks.said: Know small business application stateside versus overseas.
checks.now: Changed by the RFO: Part 19 must apply in the U.S. and outlying areas and may apply outside. Confirm DoW and command policy.

checks.said: FFP up to $500K, criteria in DFARS PGI 204.804-3.
checks.now: Not rechecked: the DFARS closeout coverage may have moved under DoW's RFO deviations. Check the current PGI.

checks.said: Elements of a contract; apparent authority not binding; FAR definition of contract.
checks.now: Same (2.101 contract definition unchanged).

checks.said: Before closing, to all who received the solicitation; after closing, to offerors not eliminated.
checks.now: Same, in FAR 15.106(a).

checks.said: Implemented as FAR number plus 200; supplemented with 70-series numbers (DFARS 201.303).
checks.now: Unchanged.

intel.t: Know the 20 FAR part titles cold
intel.d: Several questions just ask which part covers a topic. Use the RFO titles: Part 13 is Simplified Procedures for Noncommercial Acquisitions; Part 19 is Small Business.

One test taker counted about 10 questions. If the contractor must agree, bilateral; if a clause gives the Government the right (changes, options, admin, funding, termination notice), unilateral (43.203).

intel.t: UCF sections, especially B, D, H, I and M
intel.d: B = supplies or services and prices; D = packaging and marking; H = special requirements; I = clauses; M = evaluation factors. K, L and M are not physically in the contract; K is incorporated by reference.
The ninth character is the instrument type: A BPA, B IFB, C contract, D indefinite-delivery, F order, G BOA, P purchase order, Q RFQ, R RFP (4.201, Table 4-1).
Paying $5.5 million instead of $4 million means a tradeoff. The RFO adds a third approach: highest technically rated with a fair and reasonable price (15.103).
Older notes say three methods (clarifications, communications, discussions). Under the RFO: clarifications and negotiations only (15.202, 15.204-2).

Late means after the exact time. Only listed exceptions apply, and only if accepting does not unduly delay the buy; a late improvement to the winning offer can always be accepted (14.301(f), 15.107(b)).

intel.t: Certified cost or pricing data: when and when not
intel.d: Never at or below the SAT. Required at $2.5 million (FAR) or above $10 million (DoW, awards after 30 June 2026) unless adequate price competition, prices set by law, commercial, or a waiver applies.
Two or more responsible offerors competing independently. For DoW, one offer is not enough; resolicit for 30 days when the solicitation allowed fewer than 30 (DFARS 215.371-2).
Price analysis checks the total; cost analysis checks the elements and is required with certified data. Cost realism is required for cost-reimbursement contracts (15.404).
Agency, GAO, Court of Federal Claims; no required order. Solicitation defects before closing; others 10 days at GAO; agency goal 35 days; GAO 100 days (33.104, 33.105).
A protest objects to a solicitation or award; a claim is a demand by a party to an existing contract (33.102, 2.101).

intel.t: Your first action on a protest
intel.d: Consult legal counsel (33.103(a)); for agency protests notify the HCA; withhold award or suspend performance as the rules require.

intel.t: Claims and REAs: when to certify
intel.d: Claims over $100,000 must be certified (2.101). DoW also requires certification of requests for equitable adjustment over the SAT (DFARS 252.243-7002).
By definition (33.201). Policy is to resolve disputes at the contracting officer's level by agreement (33.204).
Convenience (no longer needed), default (noncommercial, contractor fault, Part 49), cause (commercial, contractor fault, 52.212-4(m)). Cure notice with 10 or more days left; show cause with fewer.
Contractors furnish their own property ordinarily (45.102). Liability for loss depends on contract type (45.104).

intel.t: Inspection, acceptance and risk of loss
intel.d: Acceptance is conclusive except latent defects, fraud and gross mistakes. Risk passes at acceptance or delivery at destination, whichever is later (46.505).
Orientation: with the winner, about performance. Debriefing: with offerors, about the evaluation; request in 3 days, held within 5 (15.301-1).

intel.t: When the source selection decision document is written
intel.d: After the comparative assessment and before award. It records the SSA's rationale and tradeoffs (15.205).
FFP 6 months after physical completion; indirect rates 36 months; all others 20 months; simplified buys on receipt and final payment (Table 4-2).
Contracts and related records: 6 years after final payment (4.309, Table 4-3).
30 days after a proper invoice or acceptance, whichever is later. 15 days for small business is a goal (32.009).
Least preferred financing. Look at private and customary financing first (32.106).
Thresholds use the final anticipated value including all options (1.107(c)).
Every authority is delegable unless the FAR says otherwise (1.107(b)). A warrant (SF 1402) states your limits (1.403-2).

intel.t: Organizational conflicts of interest and gifts
intel.d: OCI: impaired objectivity, biased advice or unfair advantage (2.101, subpart 9.5). Never solicit gifts from contractors (3.101-2).
SOW (how), PWS (outcomes and standards), SOO (objectives; offeror writes the PWS). Requirements must not unduly restrict competition (Part 11).
Required before new requirements, before solicitations over the SAT, and before orders over the SAT (10.001(b)).
EDA (in PIEE) is where DoW distributes contract documents. CBAR (DCMA) holds contractor business data and negotiation records for pricing.
Test takers describe about 80% scenarios and 20% recall. Understand why a rule exists so you can apply it to a new story.
